rationale: Evidence from iteration 7 (score 673.1, best so far, up from 600.4): raising kd from 0.8 to 1.1 with the iteration-3 geometry gave a clear gain. The oval still finishes 20/20 at 1.81 s with max_error 0.016 m. The s-bend improved to 18/20 finishes (from 14/20). The slalom progress rose from 0.23 to 0.42, the largest improvement on any track, though it still fails 20/20 with 1.8 line-loss events per run. Earlier geometry and speed changes (iterations 4-6) all hurt, so the derivative term is the lever that has helped. steering_oscillation on the s-bend rose to 0.35, but this is still acceptable and the oval's control effort fell to 2.28, which suggests the extra damping is not adding noise. Change: keep the iteration-7 geometry and every other controller value, and raise kd from 1.1 to 1.5. Hypothesis H1: slalom failure is steering lag at sharp left-right alternations, so more derivative damping keeps raising slalom progress, with a reasonable chance of pushing it past 0.6. H2: the oval and s-bend stay stable, because their gentle curves change the signal slowly. H3 (risk): at kd 1.5 sensor noise is amplified, so steering_oscillation rises above about 0.45 on the s-bend and the oval loses completions. If that happens, the next step is kd about 1.3, or testing sensor_size 0.012 for the slalom. Expected result: slalom progress 0.5 or more with line_loss_events below 1.2, s-bend at 18/20 or better, and oval time near 1.8 s. Next measurements: slalom progress and line_loss_events, s-bend completion and off-track count, steering_oscillation and max_error on all tracks, and noise_robustness to check whether noise is becoming the limit.
